messages:
Maria: nightly-bot just flagged a regression on xsmall-v2-int8 from the multi-workload nightly. Short-answer promptset A fail rate +18% vs fp32, hallucination up, and early stopseqs increased. attaching the diff report.
nightly-bot: auto-report: https://ci.redwood.ai/runs/1712509876/xsmall-v2-int8/diff — metrics: short_answer_acc -0.18, hallucination_rate +0.12, avg_latency +0.01
Rahul: can someone paste quant config + build args? need to know if per-channel vs per-tensor was used and whether layernorm folding happened.
Tara: was the tokenizer pinned to the same commit when we built int8? last time token-id remap caused short generations.
James: checked the quant config in the job: ```
# quant args
quant_backend: ptq
per_channel: true
calib_samples: 1024
fold_layernorm: true
clip_range: 6.0
```
James: looked at logits diff for one failing prompt — fold_layernorm + per_channel seems to change scale of pre-softmax scores in later layers, pushing EOS above threshold earlier.
Linh: I repro'd locally with the same binary. Example:
Prompt: "List three causes of data drift"
fp32 toks: [101, 42, 73, 99, 2, ... ] -> no EOS until token 40
int8 toks: [101, 42, 73, 2] -> EOS emitted at token 4
Linh: token id 2 is EOS for this tokenizer variant; looks like tokenization / detokenization mismatch combined with scale change.
Rahul: so this looks like a conjunction of: (1) tokenizer commit mismatch, (2) layernorm folding + per-channel quant shift, (3) our gating didn't include token-level alignment checks.
Maria: immediate mitigation: roll back the xsmall-v2-int8 rollout on hosted and dedicated. block other models using the same quant packing until we validate.
opsbot: rollback scheduled: will revert promotion: xsmall-v2-int8 -> stable at 1712509950. Canary traffic will be cut and previous fp32 binary restored.
Tara: longer-term actions I propose:
- Add token-level alignment test to nightly: compare token sequence length and first-EOS position vs fp32 baseline across promptset A/B. fail if mean EOS_pos delta > 2 tokens or >10% of prompts.
- Add a quant-sensitivity check during onboarding: run a small set of structured-output prompts (QA + list + code) and assert no hallucination-rate regression > 5%.
- Pin tokenizer commit in model bundle; add sanity check in build that vocab hash matches baseline.
James: short-term technical patch: try disabling fold_layernorm in the PTQ pipeline and retest — hypothesis: folding + per-channel scale is amplifying rounding effects that expose tokenizer mismatch.
Linh: also add a deterministic detokenize test: for 500 random prompts, run tokenization->detokenization roundtrip and assert exact string equality.
Rahul: gating rule draft:
- Onboard-int8 gating requires passing: token_alignment, hallucination <= baseline +5%, short_answer_acc drop <=2%, and regression-free on promptset A,B.
- If any gating fails, block promotion and create a triage thread.
Maria: owners & ETA:
- rollback + customer ops notice: opsbot (done) / ETA: now
- immediate hotfix attempt (disable fold_layernorm): James / ETA: 4h
- tokenizer pin + roundtrip tests in CI: Tara / ETA: 24h
- gating rule + nightly add: Rahul / ETA: 48h
- follow-up postmortem doc: Maria / ETA: EOD tomorrow
James: FYI I'll push a canary build with fold_layernorm=false and run the nightly subset locally, will post results here.
Linh: I'll run the detokenize roundtrip and share failing examples; if we have a tokenizer commit mismatch I'll open a patch to pin the model bundle.
Maria: thanks all. labeling this thread: regression-int8-tokenizer-layernorm; will track actions in the follow-up postmortem. :white_check_mark:
